name: Chile
headline: Chile: +2.5% growth in 2025, 4.2% inflation, debt 42% of GDP
sections: Chile is a $357 billion economy (2025), the world's 46th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +2.5% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $38K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 9.0% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 4.2% in 2025, above typical targets, down from 11.6% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 8.5% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 21.6% (2025).
Gross government debt is 42% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has risen from 32% in 2020. The general government balance is −2.8% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is −1.2% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 65% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 4.1% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 49% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 81.4 years (2024). Population: 20.0 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
